articles.headline: Preseason Bracketology: Utah St. Takes the Top Line, Kentucky Sneaks In, and Houston Waits Outside
articles.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ, and welcome to the first bracket of the new season. Nothing has been played, so there are no records and no results to lean on. This field comes from the same blend the sim uses to start the year (40% of each team's final rating from last season, 60% of its new tier rating) plus a handful of calls from me. Every one of those calls is logged as a committee adjustment on the Bracketology Board, so you can see what I did and argue with it.

THE TOP LINE
Utah St. is my No. 1 overall seed, and that is the boldest call on the board. Virginia is the defending champion and still has the best blended rating, but the Aggies went 32-3 with the best scoring margin outside Virginia, lost in the second round to a team that played the game of its life, and I'm not going to let one afternoon decide the preseason. Virginia is the other No. 1 seed, along with Seton Hall and Alabama. Seton Hall gets a bump for being the national runner-up and the No. 2 team in the committee poll; the Pirates would not be a No. 1 seed on rating alone, but they would not be much of a surprise either. Texas, Florida, Purdue and San Diego State make up the 2 line.

THE AUTO-BIDS
As always, I'm picking who I think cuts down the nets, not who won last year. Virginia gets the ACC, Alabama the SEC over Florida, Purdue the Big 10, Seton Hall the Big East and Utah St. the Mountain West. San Diego State is in as an at-large. Texas Tech and Baylor rate level in the Big 12, so I gave the bid to the Red Raiders and the at-large to the Bears. UAB takes the American over Memphis, and St. Louis, which went 29-3, takes the A-10 and becomes a 6 seed on a +3 adjustment.

THE FIELD
The power leagues dominate again: the Big 12 has nine teams, the ACC, SEC and Big 10 have eight each, the Big East has five and the Mountain West four. The last four in are Kentucky, Memphis, Colorado and NC State, who would open in Dayton. Kentucky is the other bold call. The Wildcats went 11-20 last year, and they are in on a +4 adjustment because I'm betting a blue blood bounces back.

THE ABSENTEES
Houston is the first team out. At 8-23 last year it should not be this close, but the +8 adjustment I gave it puts it right on the line, and a good start would move it into the field. VCU, Ohio St. and Georgetown round out the first four out; UCLA, Oregon, Miami and Auburn are the next four. On the other side, I'm fading Michigan St. (a 9 seed), Arizona (a 7) and Illinois (an 8). The Spartans went to the Elite Eight as a 22-15 team, and I don't trust it to happen twice.

WHAT TO WATCH
Ratings will move quickly. Teams get to 10 games before their results count fully, so the early bracket is mostly about reputation, and it will look very different in three weeks. Watch Kentucky and Houston in particular, since they are the two teams I'm asking you to believe in without much evidence. See you next week.

articles.headline: Week 1: Alabama Takes the Top Line, VCU Crashes the Bracket, and Utah St. Falls One Point Short
articles.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Three days are in the books, roughly 290 games, and the preseason bracket has already been reshuffled. Here is the new field, who moved, and what I'm not sure about yet.

THE TOP LINE
Alabama is my No. 1 overall seed. The Crimson Tide are 2-0 with wins of 107-58 and 117-52, the best offense in the field so far. Virginia, Seton Hall and Texas join them. Texas climbs a line after wins over Troy and Northwestern by an average of 37.

Utah St. is the story at the top. The preseason No. 1 overall opened with wins of 90-64 and 100-55 and then lost 85-84 at Indiana on Day 3. That is a one-point loss to a good team, and it is why I moved the Aggies down only to a 2 seed rather than further. San Diego State, a 1-0 team after a 109-62 win over Yale, takes the Mountain West auto-bid.

THE BIGGEST MOVER
VCU is the biggest mover on the board. The Rams are 3-0 and beat Michigan 107-58 and Illinois-Chicago 112-48, and they are in as the A-10 auto-bid and a 4 seed. They were outside the field last week. Michigan is out because of that loss, and it only beat Maine by one.

THE FALLERS
Purdue only escaped Cleveland State 77-76 on the last possession after a six-point win over Creighton, and drops from a 2 seed to a 5. Missouri lost 75-63 to San Francisco in its opener. Tennessee lost to Pepperdine, BYU to Louisiana-Monroe and USC to Middle Tennessee, and all three have lost ground. Xavier lost at home to Richmond. Indiana is the odd one: it beat Utah St. but lost to Radford on Day 1.

THE FIELD
The Big 12 has nine teams, the SEC eight, the ACC and Big 10 seven, the Big East five and the Mountain West four. The last four in are NC State, Houston, Ohio St. and Marquette, who would open in Dayton. Houston, my preseason first team out, moves in after a 78-75 win over Monmouth. The first four out are Louisville, Michigan, Georgetown and Mississippi State.

THE AUTO-BIDS
Cleveland State gets the Horizon bid over IU Indy, which has lost to UMBC and Drake. Arkansas-Pine Bluff replaces Southern in the SWAC, and Northeastern keeps the CAA despite losing to San Jose State.

WHAT TO WATCH
Ratings are still mostly preseason numbers, so everything here is provisional. Teams are 10 games away from counting fully, and I expect more movement next week. Watch Utah St. and Purdue, who both have something to prove.

articles.headline: Week 2: Gonzaga Climbs to the Top Line, Michigan Barely Hangs On, and the Bubble Churns
articles.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Six days and 604 games are in, and most teams now have three to five games. Here is the new field.

THE TOP LINE
Alabama stays No. 1 overall at 3-0, with wins of 49, 65 and 20 points. The surprise is Gonzaga, which jumps three lines to a 1 seed. The Zags are 5-0 and have beaten Indiana 107-61 and Arkansas-Pine Bluff 95-65. Texas (4-0, including an 87-80 win over Iowa St.) and San Diego State (3-0) are the other No. 1 seeds. Virginia drops a line to a 2, and Seton Hall, 2-0 with the thinnest résumé of the top group, drops two lines to a 3. Utah St. is at 4-1 and holds a 2 seed; its only loss is the one-pointer at Indiana.

THE RISERS
New Hampshire is 5-1 and the best team in the America East by a mile; it climbs from a 12 to a 6. Pepperdine, 4-0 with wins over Tennessee and Memphis, jumps from a 12 to an 8. Wofford, Saint Peter's and Yale are all ahead of where they started. Georgetown, Rutgers and Mississippi State are in the field for the first time.

THE FALLERS
Purdue lost 83-72 to Baylor on Day 6 and slides to a 7 seed after two close calls against Creighton and Cleveland State. Kentucky is out. The Wildcats lost 79-61 to UTSA on Day 6 and the bold preseason pick is not holding up. Memphis (1-2, losses to Pepperdine and Bradley), Ohio St. (1-2) and Marquette (lost 90-89 to San Jose State) are out as well. Indiana falls four lines after a 107-61 loss to Gonzaga and a Day 1 loss to Radford, even though it beat Utah St.

THE FIELD
The Big 12 has nine teams, the SEC and Big 10 eight each, the ACC seven, the Big East five and the Mountain West four. The last four in are Houston, Mississippi State, Rutgers and Indiana, who would open in Dayton. Michigan, which lost 107-58 to VCU, is the last at-large in, so the Wolverines are on thin ice. The first four out are Louisville, Stanford, Dayton and New Mexico.

THE AUTO-BIDS
Winthrop has the Big South's best rating despite a 1-2 start. Cleveland State, 0-3, is still the Horizon's best rating, which says more about the league than about the Vikings.

WHAT TO WATCH
Teams will have about ten games by the end of next week, which is the point where their results start to count fully. A lot of this bracket still reflects preseason reputations, and I expect a lot of seed changes next week.

articles.headline: Week 3: The Power Leagues Are Piling Up Wins, Syracuse and Butler Join the Field, and Kentucky Is Back
articles.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Nine days and 892 games are in. Most teams have played between three and seven times, and the biggest story is something I didn't see coming in November: the unbeaten list is full of power-conference teams.

THE BIG STORY: UNBEATEN POWER TEAMS
Fifty-four teams are still undefeated. Twenty-nine of them come from the ACC, Big 12, Big 10, SEC and Big East, which have 79 teams between them. The list includes the usual favorites, but it also includes teams that finished the year in the middle of the pack. Georgetown (17-14 last season) is 4-0. Iowa (19-12) is 6-0. Syracuse (18-13) is 5-0, with a 76-63 win over South Carolina. Butler (14-18) is 4-0 and beat Penn State 75-73. Oklahoma State (16-16) is 3-0. NC State (19-12) is 3-1 and lost only at Seton Hall. TCU (18-14) is 5-2, with both losses on the road to Florida State and Vanderbilt. None of those seven teams won more than 19 games last year.

WHY IT'S HAPPENING
Part of it is real: the power leagues are 221-67 against everyone else, a .767 winning percentage, and the teams from the top of those leagues have simply been better than the field. But a lot of it is the schedule. Those 29 unbeaten power teams have 120 wins between them, and only 18 are against power-conference opponents. Another 101 are against teams outside my top 100. That's not a knock on the teams; it's the nature of the first 20 days, which are non-conference games against random opponents. A 5-0 start against teams I don't rate means a 5-0 start against teams I don't rate.

HOW I'M TREATING IT
I'm not moving them up much yet. My board is built mostly from ratings, and wins over low-rated teams don't move a rating. Syracuse and Butler get a small bump and are in the field as a 10 seed and a First Four team. Iowa moves to an 8, Georgetown to a 7, and NC State slides to a 10 after its first loss. Oklahoma State (3-0 with wins over Houston Christian, Boston University and Utah Tech) and TCU are not in, and I want to see them beat someone good first.

WHAT THIS DOES TO THE FIELD AND THE SEASON
The days ahead matter. Conference play starts on Day 21, and every conference game has a winner and a loser. The 79 power-conference teams will win about as many league games as they lose, so the unbeaten list is going to shrink fast. A team that starts 10-0 and finishes 10-10 in the league is a bubble team, not a lock. I expect a crowded bubble of 19- and 20-win teams with middling conference records, and in my current field 32 of the 37 at-large spots already belong to power-league teams, so the pressure falls on the mid-majors. That means a team like Bradley (5-0, a 12 seed) or Pepperdine (6-0, a 7 seed) will need a lot more than a gaudy record to hold its place. Quality wins and bad losses are going to decide the field, and right now there are very few of either.

THE REST OF THE BOARD
Alabama is the overall No. 1 for a third week. Gonzaga (6-0) and Utah St. (6-1, with an 88-69 win over Virginia Tech) are on the top line with Texas, and Seton Hall (4-0, 91-74 over NC State) is a 2 seed. Kentucky is back in the field at 4-1 as a 12 seed. Houston is out after losses to UMass-Lowell and Le Moyne, and Colorado State is out after losing 87-62 to Southeastern Louisiana, a 16 seed. The last four in are Michigan, Ohio St., Rutgers and Butler. The first four out are St. John's, Grand Canyon, Indiana and Dayton.

WHAT TO WATCH
Days 10 through 20 finish the non-conference slate. After that, the schedule gets real. Keep an eye on Syracuse, Butler and Georgetown: if they are still unbeaten when conference play begins, I'll be wrong about how good they are.

articles.headline: Week 4: The Unbeaten List Shrinks, Syracuse, Butler and Kentucky Fall Out, and the Mid-Majors Take Back Four Spots
articles.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Twelve days and 1,198 games are in. Last week I wrote that the unbeaten list was full of power-conference teams and that it wouldn't stay that way. It is already shrinking: 43 teams are still undefeated, down from 54, and 24 of them are from the ACC, Big 12, Big 10, SEC and Big East, down from 29.

THE TOP OF THE BOARD
Alabama (7-0) is the overall No. 1 seed for the fourth straight week. Gonzaga (7-0), San Diego State (6-0, a 111-72 win over Saint Peter's) and Utah St. (7-1) join it on the top line. Texas, Seton Hall, Virginia and Texas Tech are the 2 seeds. Florida State beat Iowa St. 83-64, and the Cyclones (5-2) fall to a 5 seed.

THE FALLEN
Syracuse, Butler and Kentucky are all out. Syracuse lost 94-82 at East Carolina on Day 10, its first loss, and Butler lost 81-73 to Saint Peter's on Day 11. Kentucky (4-2) lost 71-66 to Louisiana-Monroe, and Ohio St. (3-3) lost 90-76 to Louisville. Illinois lost 86-79 to Kansas and 91-63 to Iowa St., and falls from a 9 seed to a 13. Purdue lost 67-66 to Tennessee, its second loss.

THE SURVIVORS
Georgetown (6-0), Iowa (7-0), Pittsburgh (7-0) and NC State (5-1) all hold 8 and 9 seeds. West Virginia and Arizona are also still unbeaten. Oklahoma State is 4-0, but it still has not beaten a team I rate, and TCU lost again (5-3). Villanova is the big mover: 7-1 and up from a 10 to a 7.

I SAID THE SQUEEZE WAS COMING. THE FIELD SAYS OTHERWISE, FOR NOW
Last week I thought the power leagues would take even more of the at-large bids as their records piled up. It hasn't gone that way. Thirty-three of the 68 teams in my field are from the five power leagues, down from 37, and 28 of the 37 at-large bids, down from 32. The reason is the one I gave: wins over teams I don't rate don't move a rating. Syracuse, Butler and Kentucky had the records, but they didn't have the quality, and as soon as they lost to teams of similar level, they were out. Meanwhile mid-majors with better numbers have moved in. Princeton is 10-0, the best record in the field, and is in as an at-large. San Francisco and Grand Canyon are both in. Memphis (5-2) is the American's auto-bid, and West Georgia (7-0) takes the ASUN's from Queens.

The season is still pointed the same way. Conference play starts on Day 21, and the power leagues will play 20 games against each other. Their records will collapse toward .500, and the bubble will be decided by who wins those games.

THE LAST FOUR IN AND OUT
The last four in are Michigan St., San Francisco, Rutgers and Princeton. The first four out are Colorado State, Marquette, Wyoming and Stanford, followed by Queens, Butler, Louisville and St. John's.

THE AUTO-BIDS
Utah Valley (6-4) has the WAC's best rating after Southern Utah lost three straight. Southern (6-0) is back as the SWAC's auto-bid. Cleveland State, 3-5, still has the Horizon's best rating, which says more about the league than about the Vikings.

THE CRAZIEST THINGS I'VE SEEN SO FAR
Start with Indiana, which is the strangest team in the country. The Hoosiers lost 73-71 to Radford on Day 1, the biggest upset of the year by my ratings, and then beat Utah St. 85-84 two days later. That makes Utah St.'s only loss a one-point defeat to a team that lost to Radford. Brown beat Oklahoma 87-81, Long Island beat Saint Joseph's, and UMass-Lowell beat Houston 89-74, which is why Houston fell out of the field. The blowouts are just as wild: Utah St. beat Utah 113-41, Gonzaga beat Weber State 124-56, and Bradley beat Tulane 104-38. Texas beat Prairie View A&M 133-80, and Prairie View then lost to Siena 100-94, a 194-point game. At the other end, Coppin State beat Delaware 56-32 and Army 62-38. Nearly one game in five (229 of 1,198) has been decided by 30 or more points, and home teams are winning 58.5% of the time.

THE UNBEATEN WATCH: HOW MANY CAN SURVIVE?
Forty-three teams are unbeaten now. Using my ratings and the engine's typical 13.5-point spread on a single game, my rough model says about 1.5 teams will get through the regular season unbeaten, and about a 13% chance that nobody does. Treat that as an upper bound, because last year's best team lost a game in its 30 and the model isn't built to see that coming. Gonzaga (7-0) has the easiest path, Alabama (7-0) is next, and Navy (7-0) is the surprise third. It's worth asking what the committee would do with an unbeaten mid-major. A 30-0 Navy would be a 3 or 4 seed on my board, not a 1, because it has few quality wins to show for the record. That is the cost of a soft slate, and it's why I put Gonzaga on the top line and Navy on the 9.

THE COLLISIONS COMING
The schedule is about to do my job for me. Texas (5-0) visits Texas Tech (6-0) on Day 13, the first meeting of two unbeaten power teams, so one of them has a loss by tomorrow night. Virginia (5-0) visits Seton Hall (6-0) on Day 18. In the Mountain West, UNLV and San Diego State, both 6-0, play on Days 30 and 31, back to back. And Alabama's finish may be the best of the year: it hosts Florida on Day 27 and Arkansas on Day 38, then plays at Florida on Day 40 and at Texas on Day 41. If the Crimson Tide are unbeaten going into that stretch, they will have to win two straight SEC road games on the last two days of the regular season.

THE LEAGUE RANKINGS NOBODY ASKED FOR
Averaging every team's rating on my board, the SEC is the best league (15.5), then the Big 12 (13.0), the Mountain West (12.5), the Big East (11.7), the ACC (10.1) and the Big 10 (10.0). Two things stand out. First, the Mountain West is third and has four teams in the field, and could end up with more. Second, the Big 10, with 18 teams and seven bids, is the weakest of the big six by average rating. If its middle doesn't improve, expect it to lose a bid or two in the weeks ahead, most likely to the Mountain West or the WCC.

THE HYPOTHETICAL
Suppose Texas beats Texas Tech tomorrow, Alabama goes unbeaten through the 20-game SEC schedule, and Gonzaga does the same in the WCC. Then my No. 1 overall seed is a coin flip between an unbeaten Gonzaga and an unbeaten Alabama, and I'd probably give it to Alabama because the SEC schedule is harder. If instead the Tide lose at Florida on Day 40, Gonzaga becomes the obvious No. 1, and for the first time this year the top line would have a team from outside the power leagues.

WHAT TO WATCH
Eight more days of non-conference games and then conference play begins. Watch Texas at Texas Tech on Day 13, whether Navy and Gonzaga are still unbeaten when Day 21 arrives, and the Big 10 bubble. Most of the movement from here on will be on the bubble.
